what: How each surface reads the sixteen stored task and calendar preferences, resolves a list’s effective coupling, auto-date and carry-over, and normalises what it writes back: the countdown window, the visible day window and the per-list override map. Measured on the real code of both surfaces before the port.
why: The desktop TaskCascadeProvider and the mobile taskBehaviour.ts each parse these values with their own copy of every rule, and the synced prefs mean each device reads what the other wrote. One reader in the core answers the same for both, and for a frontend that is not JavaScript.
writtenBy: src/state/taskSettings.measure.test.tsx — a one-off, run once and deleted. It rendered the desktop provider with its preference reads answered from the case, and ran the mobile module with its preference module answered the same way; where the two surfaces answered differently, the row carries both (`expect` is mobile’s, `desktop` the desktop’s) and `surfacesDiffer`.

whereItLives.note: Inside cal-core, beside the day-start tables.

notInThisTable.the settings screens: what each control offers and how it announces a change
notInThisTable.when to write: the desktop’s debounced write that stays silent when the value did not move, the re-read after a sync round, and the mobile writes’ best-effort catch are the platform’s
notInThisTable.host-core’s reading of tasks.dayStartTri: reminders::day_start_time reads any HH:MM (seconds allowed) and garbage as midnight, where both surfaces read only the five offered values; an open decision, see the day-start table
notInThisTable.priorityScale: the two-level switch as a scale name, a one-line mapping

shape.keys: the stored keys, by the names the cases use
shape.prefs: stored values by key; a key not given is not stored
shape.expect: what mobile holds (reads and effective settings), or the string mobile writes
shape.desktop: present only where the desktop answered differently
shape.Num: "NaN", "Infinity" and "-Infinity" stand for the numbers JSON cannot spell
shape.wasTypeScript: a row pinning a JavaScript artifact a port may decide against, and must then change on purpose

read.name: an-on-knob-turns-off-only-on-a-literal-false
read.note: Default-on knobs: only the exact string "false" turns one off; any other spelling, or nothing, leaves it on.

read.name: countdown-days-a-decimal-is-cut
read.note: parseInt reads the digits before the point.

read.name: countdown-days-trailing-garbage-is-ignored
read.note: parseInt stops at the first non-digit.

read.name: a-window-edge-between-half-hours-snaps
read.note: 435 minutes is 14.5 half hours; it rounds up to 450.

read.name: a-trigger-off-the-list-is-midnight
read.note: Only app-start, 00:00, 06:00, 08:00 and 12:00 are read; a valid time that is not offered falls back to 00:00. host-core’s reminders read the same key as any HH:MM.

read.name: an-entry-that-is-not-an-object-is-dropped
read.note: An array passes the object check but has none of the fields, so it drops as empty.

read.name: fields-of-the-wrong-type-are-dropped
read.note: No string for a boolean, no number, no carry-over spelled otherwise; an entry left with nothing is dropped.

read.name: a-repeated-list-keeps-the-last
read.note: JSON.parse keeps the last of two equal keys.

read.name: a-list-named-proto-is-lost
read.note: Assigning to "__proto__" on a plain object sets its prototype instead of a field, so the entry is not kept. A JavaScript artifact; a port that keeps the list must then change this row on purpose.

read.name: one-failed-read
read.note: The surfaces differ. Mobile reads all keys in one Promise.all behind one catch, so one failed read makes EVERY setting the default; the desktop catches each read, so only that key falls back.

effective.name: an-override-wins-per-field
effective.note: L1 overrides only the coupling; auto-date and carry-over come from the globals.

effective.name: a-list-named-constructor-without-an-override-inherits
effective.note: Looking up "constructor" on a map without it finds Object.prototype.constructor, whose fields are all absent.

effective.name: a-list-named-proto-finds-its-override-through-the-prototype
effective.note: The entry was not kept as a field (see the read row), yet looking up "__proto__" returns the map’s prototype, which IS that entry, so its coupling applies after all. A JavaScript artifact; a port that keeps "__proto__" as an ordinary list id answers the same here and must then change the read row on purpose.

countdownWrite.name: infinity-is-written-as-the-default
countdownWrite.note: Not finite, so the default, not the upper clamp.

overrideUpdate.name: an-update-keeps-its-place
overrideUpdate.note: The key order is what the stored JSON is compared by.

overrideUpdate.name: fields-are-written-in-a-fixed-order
overrideUpdate.note: Coupling, auto-date, carry-over, whatever order they were given in.

overrideUpdate.name: a-list-named-proto
overrideUpdate.note: The surfaces differ: the desktop builds `{ ...prev, [listId]: trimmed }`, where a computed key makes a real field; mobile assigns `next[listId] = trimmed`, which sets the prototype. A JavaScript artifact either way.
